display_name: Y Combinator post-money SAFE (Simple Agreement for Future Equity), and the Pro Rata Side Letter
authority: NONE — a standard form has a publisher, not an enacting authority. Y Combinator publishes it; no legislature or agency promulgated it, and no gazette carries it.

source.asset_host: The download links on that page point at //bookface-static.ycombinator.com/assets/ycdc/<name>-<64 hex>.<ext>. The same paths under https://www.ycombinator.com/assets/ycdc/ serve byte-identical files; both were re-fetched on 2026-09-04 and every sha256 matched the deposited copy. The `url` on each form below is the www form.
source.note: The publisher's own page. It lists exactly the ten instruments deposited here plus the User Guide; there is no other edition or variant offered.

governing_law.note: Per canon's directory conventions §3, governing law is a subject field rather than a path component, because for a contract it is a term of the instrument. This form makes the point sharply: it is a BLANK on the US forms and FIXED on two of the three non-US forms, so the subject has no single value. The per-form facts are in `forms[].governing_law`.
governing_law.us: blank — the parties fill in a State
governing_law.ca: federal laws of Canada, plus a province the parties fill in

product_matrix.note: Six SAFEs, not twelve. The publisher offers no discount or MFN form for Singapore, Canada or the Cayman Islands; those five cells do not exist. Synthesising one would produce exactly the 'modified version' the licence footer asks people not to disseminate.

editions.authority: SAFE User Guide, Appendix III, 'Summary of Substantive Changes in the Post-Money Safe' (source/docx/SAFE User Guide.pdf). Appendix III states: 'Version numbers are stamped on the upper right-hand corner of each form of the post-money safe.' The stamps as measured are in source/footers.json and in forms[].version_stamp.

changes: Statement that neither party has changed the safe form except to fill in blanks and bracketed terms (Preamble, second paragraph).
The safe is expressly copyrighted and made available under the Creative Commons Attribution-No Derivatives 4.0 License (first page footer).
Deletion of the post-conversion round pro rata right; addition of the optional Pro Rata Side Letter (Section 1(a); Pro Rata Side Letter).
Safe holder's payout choices in a Liquidity Event are indifferent to the form of consideration (Section 1(b)).
The safe's priority is confirmed to be on par with standard preferred stock (Section 1(d)).

Company Capitalization redefined: this safe and other safes included; the Equity Financing option pool increase excluded; Unissued Option Pool and Promised Options specifically included (definition of 'Company Capitalization'). This is the change that makes the cap operate post-money.

Liquidity Capitalization redefined: safes included except those taking Cash-Out Amounts or similar liquidation preference; Promised Options included only to the extent receiving Proceeds (definition of 'Liquidity Capitalization').

Investor Representations add an acknowledgment that the company may rescind the safe by returning the Purchase Amount if the holder is not accredited at the Equity Financing (Section 4(b), first sentence).
A majority-in-interest may amend the safe (Section 5(a)).
Dividend rights on the safe's as-converted ownership (Section 5(c) and the definition of 'Dividend Amount').
Removal of the valuation-cap-and-discount version of the post-money safe. The description was removed from the User Guide's Appendix I and the form was concurrently removed from the YC website.

list.release_date_precision: month; Appendix III says 'Release Date February 2023' and gives no day
changes: 'Safe Preferred Stock' redrafted to refer to liquidation multiple (Section 2).
The assignment provision no longer carries the proviso about a change of company domicile (Section 5(d)).
In the MFN form, 'Subsequent Convertible Securities' is redrafted to exclude side letters (Section 2).

editions.anomaly: The MFN form deposited here is stamped 'Version 1.3'. Appendix III's changelog stops at 1.2 and describes no 1.3, and the User Guide's own Q7 quotes that form's header as 'MFN ONLY Version 1.1'. So the MFN instrument has been revised at least twice since the text of the guide was written, and at least once since the last changelog entry, with no published note of what changed. Nothing here reconstructs the diff: only the stamp is evidence. Do not read '1.3' as covered by the 1.2 changelog.
editions.deposited: The five cap and discount forms are stamped 1.2 (the three non-US ones as 'Singapore Version 1.2', 'Canada Version 1.2', 'Cayman Version 1.2'); the MFN form is stamped 1.3; the US Pro Rata Side Letter is stamped 'Version 1.0'; the three non-US side letters carry no stamp at all.
